semantic_roundtrip.remaining_semantic_delta: The source Algorithm 2.2 supporting-vector choice is implemented as a deterministic finite-history function. Finite-dimensional coordinate-free geometry and shared exact projection realize its update. Played-point support legality is sufficient; the stronger off-path oracle law is an optional adapter. The fixed-step bound covers T=0 as an explicit library extension, the variable bound uses a diameter upper bound, and tuning uses a distance bound for one known positive horizon. Total prefix/canonical equalities remain distinct from performance. One fixed deterministic policy receives whole past and current losses and actual finite output histories. Performance assumes global support legality at the actual played points; the stronger off-path oracle law is optional. Canonical identities and strict-past equality are total even on invalid inputs and alone imply no regret guarantee. Fixed-step bounds retain initial feasibility and a negative terminal distance, including the derived T=0 branch. Variable bounds require positive nonincreasing rates and a diameter bound. Tuned statements concern a single known positive horizon and one constant-step run shared by its fixed comparators. No bandit feedback, randomized-law semantics, executable oracle, parameter-independence, anytime tuning, attained best-hindsight minimum, chapter/book completion, purification or Exposition Seal is asserted.
